mainText:
Wales have beaten the All Blacks for the first time in seventy three years, winning thirty five to twenty eight in Cardiff. Here is today's news.

New Zealand.

RNZ chief executive Paul Thompson has confirmed his early departure, with Head of News Mark Stevens taking over as acting chief executive from Tuesday. Former board member Jane Wrightson says she knew ministerial approval was needed for a five million dollar overdraft but cannot explain why it was never sought. The board says it was assured approval was not required. RNZ faces an eleven point eight million dollar shortfall, projected to cost fifty eight positions by next March.

Christopher Luxon will attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China next week in a caretaker capacity, with the government making formal arrangements around the caretaker status. Coalition talks continue, with the final vote count still around three weeks away. Sir Geoffrey Palmer has called the seat overhang constitutionally sad and wants it halted. Constitutional experts have drafted a letter calling for a select committee inquiry into MMP. An expert says nothing stops negotiations starting now despite the wait for special votes.

Police in Dargaville are investigating after two men used a crowbar to break into a Woolworths on Victoria Street about five thirty a.m. In Whangārei, a motorcyclist died while fleeing police, and three occupants of a car he was involved with suffered non serious injuries. At Kariotahi Beach, four people have been rescued and one remains missing. Police say one person is in serious but stable condition.

In the Bay of Plenty, Dallas Hohua, who stabbed a friend to death after a party, has had his manslaughter sentence reduced and may serve as little as two years. The byelection triggered by Western Bay of Plenty councillor Alan Kurtovich's resignation continues. Kurtovich says the Māori wards decision was absolutely the reason he quit.

Businesses hit by last week's Microsoft outage may have grounds for insurance claims, a lawyer says, with the economic impact potentially running into billions of dollars. Separately, Auckland Airport travellers can fly as planned after the E tū union withdrew a strike notice.

World.

Microsoft says Outlook, Teams and Copilot services are now fully restored after a day long global outage last week that hit the National Health Service, schools, police forces and governments from the United States to Australia. The company says the fault was technical, not a cyber incident.

A Microsoft Outlook outage last week has sharpened government focus on critical infrastructure protection, with officials privately calling it a burning issue. Officials say that work is now a priority but will take at least a year.

A copper wire network upgrade in a remote part of the United States triggered the nationwide flight ground stop last week, the US transport secretary says, with disruption expected to continue for days, including into the Thanksgiving travel rush.

Jensen Huang, who quit as Nvidia chief executive last week over revelations of an affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, has been summoned to testify before Congress. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says several government agencies had favoured blacklisting chip trading firm Megaspeed for months. Colette Kress remains interim chief executive while the board searches for a permanent successor.

Italy has fined Meta eight hundred and five million euros for failing to tell twenty million users it had access to their photos. The United States has floated Ukraine ceding the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, Volodymyr Zelensky says, though Washington has not confirmed the comments and Zelensky has rejected ceding territory.

A tanker collision with a cruise ship in New Orleans has been dubbed the miracle on the Mississippi, with all passengers rescued and thirty two people in hospital with non critical injuries.

Technology.

SpaceX will make a second attempt to catch its Starship rocket, after an earlier attempt saw the booster come down in the ocean instead of being caught.

Thousands protested in Edinburgh against artificial intelligence data centres, marching from the Royal Mile to the Scottish Parliament. The demonstrations reflect growing public concern over the scale and environmental cost of AI infrastructure being built across the United Kingdom.

Sport.

Rugby. Wales beat the All Blacks thirty five to twenty eight in Cardiff, their first win over New Zealand since nineteen fifty three. Captain Beauden Barrett says his side ran into a Welsh brick wall on defence. All Blacks coach Dave Rennie's side will review their performance this week. In other Nations Championship action, England beat Japan seventy eight to fifteen at Twickenham, Will Joseph scoring five tries on his return from four years out of the test game.

League. The Kiwis and Kiwi Ferns play the Kangaroos and Jillaroos in the Rugby League World Cup finals in Brisbane on Sunday. Isaiah Papali'i says both sides must let emotion give way to execution in the final.

Cricket. The Black Caps beat India by two hundred and forty four runs in the fourth One Day International at Mount Maunganui, Young scoring a century and Henry taking six wickets, India's second worst ODI defeat. The series remains alive.

Formula One. Liam Lawson has been confirmed at Racing Bulls for twenty twenty seven, with analysts saying he cannot afford to relax if he wants a long term seat on the grid.

Basketball. The Breakers have signed American guard Skylar Mays, formerly of the LA Lakers, to replace the injured Parker Jackson-Cartwright for the rest of the season. The Breakers also snapped a five game losing streak with an overtime win over Brisbane, DJ Vasiljevic scoring thirty six points and Carlin Davison recording a triple double.

Triathlon. Kiwi Hayden Wilde finished third at an elite sprint race in Abu Dhabi. He has pulled out of next week's World Triathlon Cup in Tauranga.

Coming up. The Rugby League World Cup final is in Brisbane on Sunday. Christopher Luxon travels to China next week for the Asia-Pacific summit. Coalition talks continue in Wellington with the final vote count still around three weeks away.

End of flash.
